issues.description: Manual HTML entity encoding in sanitizeInput() may miss edge cases or encoding contexts (HTML attribute, JavaScript context, URL). The function only handles basic characters (<, >, ", ') but doesn't account for other XSS vectors or different encoding contexts.
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested sanitization library like DOMPurify for browser contexts or validator.js escape() for server-side. Example: import validator from 'validator'; return validator.escape(input);

issues.description: generateId() uses Math.random() which is cryptographically weak and predictable. This can lead to ID enumeration attacks where attackers guess valid user IDs based on timing and patterns.
issues.suggestion: Use cryptographically secure random generation: import crypto from 'crypto'; function generateId(): string { return `user_${crypto.randomUUID()}`; } or use crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex');

issues.description: The email validation regex /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ is overly simplistic and will accept invalid emails like 'a@b.c' or 'test@domain..com'. While not a security issue, it may lead to data quality problems.
issues.suggestion: Use a more robust email validation library like validator.js: import validator from 'validator'; export function isValidEmail(email: string): boolean { return validator.isEmail(email); }

issues.description: The validation throws generic Error objects. In production, you'd want to use custom error types or error codes to distinguish between validation failures for better error handling and user feedback.
issues.suggestion: Create custom error classes: class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; } } and throw new ValidationError('Email and name are required');

issues.description: The database query is commented out, which is appropriate for a fixture/test file. However, ensure that when implemented, proper error handling is added for database operations (connection failures, constraint violations, etc.).
issues.suggestion: When implementing, wrap in try-catch: try { await db.query(query, params); } catch (error) { logger.error('Failed to save user', error); throw new DatabaseError('Could not create user'); }

codeQuality.summary: The code demonstrates good security practices with parameterized queries and input validation. Main concerns are the use of Math.random() for ID generation (should use crypto.randomUUID()) and manual HTML sanitization that could miss edge cases (use a tested library). Overall, this is well-structured code with minor security improvements needed.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive unit tests for the sanitizeInput function to verify XSS prevention. This function has zero test coverage and is critical for security.
Replace Math.random() with crypto.randomUUID() in generateId() to prevent ID enumeration attacks and ensure cryptographically secure random generation.
Replace manual HTML sanitization with a well-tested library (DOMPurify or validator.js) to ensure all XSS vectors are properly handled across different encoding contexts.
Add unit tests for all validation branches in createUser function (missing email, missing name, invalid email format) to ensure proper error handling.
Add unit tests for isValidEmail, createUser, and saveUser functions to verify core business logic and prevent regressions.
Extract validation logic into a dedicated validateUserInput function to improve separation of concerns and testability.
Replace simplistic email regex with a robust validation library (validator.js) to improve data quality and prevent invalid emails from being accepted.
Add edge case tests for email validation (null/undefined, unicode, whitespace) and user creation (very long names, mixed-case emails, XSS in names).
Create custom error classes (ValidationError, DatabaseError) to improve error handling and provide better feedback to API consumers.
